page: OVHcloud b2-15 is a general-purpose cloud server built on the x86_64 architecture. It features 4 dedicated physical cores powered by an Intel Haswell processor running at 2.0 GHz, with 1 thread per core. The hardware configuration includes 15.0 GB of RAM, providing 3.75 GB per core, and a bundled 100 GB local SSD. It operates under the KVM hypervisor and includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Performance benchmarks indicate that the b2-15 sits on the lower end of the spectrum for compute-heavy tasks. Stress-ng single-core CPU performance is in the bottom 10 percent, while multi-core performance and Geekbench scores fall into the bottom 25 percent. However, memory performance is more balanced; the Passmark memory score, database operations, and cached small-block read-only memory bandwidth all rank in the middle 50 percent. Redis SET operations show average performance at 5.93 million operations per second, and small-model LLM inference also achieves average tier speeds.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the b2-15 offers a dedicated resource profile with a balanced vCPU-to-RAM ratio on older hardware. The primary tradeoff is the legacy Intel Haswell architecture, which lacks modern instruction sets like AVX-512 or AMX, resulting in poor performance for medium-to-large LLM inference and intensive cryptographic or physics calculations.

This server is best suited for general-purpose workloads that require dedicated CPU cores but do not demand high-performance compute. Appropriate workloads include basic database operations, lightweight web serving, Redis caching, text processing, and running small-scale utility applications.
